beats.intro: Equivalent ratios show up everywhere: in recipes, maps, and prices. [[q]]When you write two of them as equal, you get a proportion, and you can use it to find a missing number.
beats.define: Cut a circle into two equal parts and shade one. [[a]]The shaded part is one half. [[b]]Now cut a circle into four parts and shade two. [[same]]Exactly the same amount is shaded. [[eq]]So one half equals two fourths. [[def]]An equation that says two ratios are equal is called a proportion. [[forms]]You can write it with fractions, or with colons: one to two equals two to four.
beats.cross: Here's a quick test for a proportion. [[q]]Is two thirds equal to eight twelfths? [[x1]]Multiply diagonally: two times twelve is twenty-four. [[x2]]And three times eight is also twenty-four. [[eq]]The cross products are equal, so the ratios form a proportion. [[q2]]What about three quarters and four eighths? [[y1]]Three times eight is twenty-four, [[y2]]but four times four is sixteen. [[no]]The cross products are different, so they're not a proportion.
beats.why: Why does this work? [[start]]Start with two equal fractions, a over b equals c over d. [[mul]]Multiply both sides by b, and by d. [[cancel]]On the left, the b cancels. On the right, the d cancels. [[res]]What's left is a times d equals b times c: the cross products. [[rule]]Doing the same thing to both sides keeps an equation true.
beats.unknown: Now let's find a missing number. [[recipe]]A lemonade recipe uses four cups of water for every lemon. [[q]]How much water for three lemons? [[set]]Write the proportion with matching units: four cups over one lemon equals x cups over three lemons. [[x]]Here x stands for the unknown number. [[cross]]Cross-multiply: one times x equals four times three. [[ans]]So x is twelve. You need twelve cups of water. [[check]]Check: twelve over three is four over one.
beats.solve: Another one: [[q]]three quarters equals x over twelve. [[cross]]Cross-multiply: four times x equals three times twelve, which is thirty-six. [[div]]Four times what is thirty-six? Divide thirty-six by four. [[ans]]x is nine. [[see]]And indeed, multiplying three quarters by three on top and bottom gives nine twelfths.
beats.constant: Look at this table. [[t]]A swimmer does three laps in eighteen minutes, and five laps in thirty minutes. [[k1]]Eighteen divided by three is six. [[k2]]Thirty divided by five is also six. [[def]]The ratio stays the same: six minutes for every lap. That fixed number is called the constant of proportionality. [[use]]With it, you can fill in any row: eight laps take eight times six, which is forty-eight minutes.
beats.wrap: A proportion says two ratios are equal. [[w1]]Check one by comparing cross products. [[w2]]To find a missing number, write the ratios with matching units, cross-multiply, then divide. [[w3]]In a proportional table, every row has the same ratio: the constant of proportionality. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
